channel.title: Who Gives the Most AI Usage
channel.description: New articles and studies that measure and compare how much real usage AI subscriptions give: plan limits, API-equivalent value, and usage multipliers.

item.title: 16 AI coding plans compared: prices, limits, and reset rules, updated Nov 10
item.description:
Script by AI updated its comparison of 16 AI coding subscription and token-plan families on Nov 10, 2026, covering ChatGPT with Codex, Claude Code, Google Antigravity, xAI's Cursor and Grok Build, GitHub Copilot, Devin, and lower-priced multi-model options like GLM, QwenCloud, MiniMax, and OpenCode.

The tables lay out price per month, how usage is limited, and when charges increase — for example, ChatGPT Pro at $100/$200/$500 with a shared Work/Codex allowance, Claude Pro/Max/Ultra at $20/$100/$200 with 5-hour and weekly caps, Copilot's monthly AI Credits, and xAI's single weekly pool shared across Grok, Cursor, and Grok Bot.

item.title: One heavy month of Codex: $100 Pro plan covered $745 of API-priced work
item.description:
Developer Flavio Copes priced 30 days of his real Codex usage at public API rates and found his $100-a-month ChatGPT Pro plan covered $745.16 of API-equivalent work. Without prompt caching, the same month would have cost $8,234.34.

The math comes from Codex's own session logs: 11,899 model calls across 25 active days, mostly GPT-6.1 Sol, with a median call sending about 150,000 input tokens — and 98% of it cached at 5% of the input price. Caching is the whole story: output was the smallest line on the bill, and 2,024 calls went over the 272K-token long-context tier, where the API charges 2x input and 1.5x output — a surcharge subscriptions don't have.

item.title: PlanLimits dashboard compares published limits for 44 AI plans across 14 vendors, with a dated change log
item.description:
PlanLimits (aiplanlimits.dev) is a new comparison site that tracks the published usage limits and prices of 44 AI plans from 14 vendors, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, the X Subscription (Grok and Cursor), GitHub Copilot, Perplexity and Windsurf.

Every number links to the vendor's official page with the date it was last checked, and the site refuses to invent message caps that vendors don't publish. It also logs plan changes, such as Claude Max 20x becoming Ultra on Oct 30 and OpenAI doubling Pro Codex allowances on Oct 29.

It has 30 head-to-head pages, such as Claude Max vs ChatGPT Pro, which notes that neither lab publishes the size of its weekly allowance. Unlike SemiAnalysis, it doesn't measure limits itself, so it complements rather than replaces API-equivalent value testing.

item.title: Franz Geffke prices one heavy month of agentic coding across subscriptions and APIs: frontier APIs cost 15 to 110x the plans
item.description:
Developer Franz Geffke took a real heavy month of agentic coding from his tku stats (about 500M uncached input, 15B cache reads, 50M output tokens, 100K requests) and priced it across subscriptions and pay-per-token APIs as of Nov 3, 2026.

At API rates that month costs about $6,500 on Claude Opus 5.5 and $12,500 on Fable 5.1. He measured Claude Max 20x ($200) as carrying about $2,000 of API-priced usage a week, and estimates ChatGPT Pro 200 plausibly carries the whole month on GPT-6.1 Sol (about $3,000 at API rates), though OpenAI doesn't publish its weekly allowance.

His conclusion: for frontier models the API costs 15 to 110 times the subscription, while for cheaper open models (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM, Kimi via Ollama Cloud, Alibaba and others) the subscription advantage shrinks to about 2 to 4x. It complements SemiAnalysis's plan-value study with a single real workload priced end to end.

item.title: Quantslant: Claude Pro beats Opus API above ~35 short tasks/day; Max credits equal the plan price
item.description:
Quantslant's Nov 5 follow-up prices Claude Pro ($20), Max 5x ($100) and Max 20x ($200) against Claude Opus 5.5 API rates, using 120 OpenRouter prompts from Oct 24, 2026. Median short Opus task: about $0.0190; a ~30,000-token document: about $0.1675.

Break-evens vs API: Pro above ~35 short tasks a day (or ~4 long docs); Max 5x ~175/day; Max 20x ~351/day. Max plans also include monthly Claude API credits equal to the plan price ($100 / $200), claimable after 7 days with no rollover, which do not cover interactive Claude Code.

Anthropic still publishes multipliers and session/weekly windows rather than a fixed message count. This is a paper break-even from measured task costs, not a meter test of plan ceilings.

item.title: Quantslant: ChatGPT Plus beats GPT-6 Astra API above ~39 short tasks a day
item.description:
Quantslant's Nov 4 follow-up to its 768-prompt subscription-vs-API series compares ChatGPT Plus ($20) with GPT-6 Astra API pricing. Using Oct 24, 2026 OpenRouter logs at $10/$50 per million tokens, a typical short Astra task medianed about $0.0170 — so $20 buys roughly 1,175 short tasks, or about 39 a day.

Plus usually wins above that short-task pace, or at about three ~30,000-token documents a day. Plus does not include Astra in chat (only Medium/High GPT-6); Astra is available to Plus in ChatGPT Work and Codex. OpenAI still does not publish a numeric Plus message cap.

Flex/Batch halve Astra rates; the piece also sketches Sol and Luna estimates and when long multi-turn chats flip the math back toward Plus.

item.title: AI Coding Daily reads the usage meters after the same four coding prompts on every ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro model
item.description:
AI Coding Daily runs the same four coding prompts on each OpenAI and Anthropic model and effort level on the $20 plans, then reads the 5-hour and weekly meters before and after, alongside the API-price equivalent and token counts (last updated Oct 28, 2026).

In the free part of the table, GPT-6.1 Sol on ChatGPT Plus used 5% to 11% of the 5-hour limit and 1% to 2% of the weekly limit for $0.42 to $0.86 of API-equivalent work. Opus 5.5 on Claude Pro used 9% to 19% of the 5-hour limit and about 1% of the weekly limit for $1.56 to $3.12 of API-equivalent work.

So per run, Claude Pro moved its weekly meter less while doing roughly three to four times the API-priced work. The rest of the models (Astra, Terra, Luna, Sonnet, Haiku) sit behind a paid tier, and the site warns that providers change limits without notice.

item.title: arrozbot works out what $1 buys on every ~$200 AI plan from official pages: only X and Google scale better at the top
item.description:
An X article by arrozbot (Nov 2) uses only Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXSI and Google's own pricing and help pages to compute usage per dollar across tiers, prompted by Replit CEO Amjad Masad's warning about subsidized plans.

Its findings: Claude scales flat (Max is 5x Pro usage for 5x the price, Ultra 10x for 10x), the X Subscription's Ultra gives 50x Plus usage for 25x the price (2x per dollar), and Google AI Ultra 20x also reaches 2x per dollar over AI Pro. OpenAI publishes no ratio between its Pro 100, 200 and 500 tiers.

It also notes that Claude Max and Ultra and ChatGPT Pro now include API credits equal to the plan price. The piece is a paper analysis of published multiples, not a meter test, and points out that no vendor publishes the base unit those multiples apply to.

item.title: Quantslant tests 768 prompts on 7 models to find when a $20, $100 or $200 AI plan beats paying API prices
item.description:
Quantslant ran 768 prompts across Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Qwen3.8 Max, GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, measured the median API cost per task (matching its OpenRouter bill to the cent on 654 of 660 requests), and compared that with plan prices checked on Oct 24, 2026.

Main finding: $20 of API usage buys about 1,050 typical short tasks on Opus 5.5 or 1,175 on GPT-6 Astra, so a $20 plan only beats the API above roughly 35 to 39 short tasks a day. For documents of about 30,000 tokens, a $20 plan pays off at just three to four analyses a day, and the author says subscriptions usually win for agent coding in Claude Code or Codex, which the test did not measure.

It also notes no provider publishes a fixed message count; Grok, for example, only lists multipliers (Premium 4x, Super 15x, Ultra 50x of Plus). A follow-up series comparing each plan against its API is due from Nov 3. Read the full test.

item.title: Adam Holter measures cost per task on subscription plans: on $20 plans, a dollar of GPT-6.1 Sol costs 7x a dollar of Opus, but a task only 1.3x
item.description:
Adam Holter ran a set of benchmarks on his subscription plans and priced each task in plan usage, not just API-equivalent dollars. His argument is that API-equivalent value alone isn't enough, because models differ a lot in how efficiently they use tokens.

  • On $20 plans, a dollar of GPT-6.1 Sol usage costs 7x what a dollar of Opus 5.5 does, but per finished task it's only about 1.3x.
  • Sonnet 5.5 costs 2.8x what Sol does per task on the API, but only about a third as much on $20 plans.
  • GPT-6 Luna costs half what Haiku 5.5 does per task on the API, but about 3x more on plans.
  • After OpenAI's Oct 29 limit doubling, he says it "completely changes the Pareto frontier" when resets are counted. Without resets, OpenAI is roughly in line with Claude. His live charts are on mypriors.com.

These numbers come from one person's benchmark runs, not a large sample of accounts.

item.title: Wokey's live dashboard measures 513 real subscription accounts: Claude plans return about 32 to 35 times their price at API rates, ChatGPT Plus about 12 times
item.description:
Wokey's coding plan comparison converts real subscription usage into API-equivalent dollars, using limit-meter changes on 513 accounts behind its gateway, and remeasures every Monday (latest data Oct 26). A full week of Claude Max 20x ($200/mo) was worth about $1,602 at API prices (35 times its price), Claude Pro ($20) about $157 (34 times), and ChatGPT Plus with Codex ($20) about $55 (12 times).

  • Max 20x gives about 10 times Pro's weekly limit; only the 5-hour window is near 20 times (about 24 times).
  • ChatGPT Plus (Codex) value fell from $92 a week on Oct 8 to $55 on Oct 26, which Wokey marks as a confirmed 58% drop.
  • Its real-traffic Max 20x figure (about $6,944 a month) sits below SemiAnalysis's single-model maximums, and it agrees with SemiAnalysis that vendors A/B-test limits.

ChatGPT Pro $200 is still collecting data (it needs 5 accounts). Note that Wokey sells pay-as-you-go access, and these are its own measured estimates, not vendor figures. Per-vendor pages: Claude Code vs Codex limits.

item.title: SemiAnalysis: Anthropic subscriptions offer 5x+ more value than OpenAI
item.description:
SemiAnalysis measured the limits on AI subscription plans from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Cursor, Cognition, and the Chinese labs, one token type at a time. It then converted each plan into what the same usage would cost at API prices.

For the mid-tier models, Claude plans gave about 5x the API-equivalent value of OpenAI's, after OpenAI halved its $200 plan and added a $500 tier. This is the founding example for this feed.
